Monday's are really busy for us so I'm making a 'Make it Monday' post now. This afternoon I'm making Roasted Red Pepper soup w/ root vegetables, a huge batch of chicken & red grape salad (I'll reserve some to make curry chicken salad by adding raisons, curry, and shallots), and meatloaf for sandwiches during the week.

Anyone else cooking today?

Tonight I'll start by melting butter in a large cast-iron skillet, then rubbing butter and spices on a bone-in chicken breast and pouring around the chicken sliced onion, probably with a small sliced Italian pepper. I use the plastic bag from the pepper to shake the onion and pepper slices in spices, including a crushed salt that has serrano pepper spice, pepper, paprika, and ground celery. I bake it in the oven. When it comes out I take the meat off the bone and put it the bone in a waiting small pot with water, a small bay leaf, onion scraps, and peppercorns. Last time the tomato I sliced wasn't fit to eat but was fine to add to the pot later in cooking. I brought the water to a boil and then let it simmer for 2-3+ hours, depending on when I'm ready to eat it. I use the lid to only pour out the broth into a bowl with salt, an egg yolk, ground celery, and paprika.
I made lime and chili shrimp with simple saffron rice. Yummy but easy.

Embarrassingly easy. There are bags of saffron yellow rice (we got Vigo) but there is also Mahatma branded. Usually a dollar or so. Just cook according to the bag. The shrimp is just whatever is at the store, usually cooked in olive oil and chili powder, finished with a couple of fresh limes squeezed over. Total cost is around $7 for the entire meal for two depending on price of shrimp. We tend to eat simple meals :)

I'm making an easy supper, of spaghetti with sauce - the sauce is garlic, olive oil, stock, salt, basil, cherry and baby plum tomatoes and chestnut mushrooms, with a tea spoon of red pesto as I've no tomato puree. It's really nice and easy. I live on my own so when I buy a whole bulb of garlic and I've got time to kill, I deskin and crush the whole lot, then pop it into a silicone icecube tray and put it in the freezer.

The tomatoes needed used up, I heated the oil, fried the garlic, popped the tomatoes, pesto, salt and veg stock cube in a pan, fried and reduced. The added the mushrooms, a touch more pesto, and because my second sauce pan went to the great kitchen cupboard in the sky (had it 18 years, the handle fell off :o) the sauce is now in a bowl while the spaghetti is cooking.

It's a lovely easy one and a real joy to eat after a crummy day.

I was off work today, so I made a big batch of Broccoli Brie mac & cheese-- one of my partner's favorites. I made the cheese sauce from scratch with real french butter, whole milk & 2 wedges of Brie (trimmed of all rind). The brie doesn't melt/incorporated well like some other cheeses do, so one has to whisk the heck out of it to help break it up over a low/moderate heat (ugh, my whisking wrist!). Mixed the sauce with cooked pasta & broccoli, put breadcrumbs with herbs de Provence & Parmesan on the top, then baked it for about 30 min. Partner came home from work and immediately said "Ooh, what smells good?" I usually make more light/healthy food instead of heavier comfort food, but when I do, I make kick-ass, bowl-licking good comfort food! Needless to say, he was very pleased.... ;)
